Dear Director Jamison: 
 
On behalf of 705 Plantation Street Realty, LLC., I am submitting this letter as Notice to file an 
Article 80 Expanded Project Notification Form with the Boston Planning and Development Agency 
(BPDA) in connection with the proposed redevelopment at 1208C VFW Parkway, West Roxbury 
(the Site). 
The Site has an area of 53,644 square feet and is currently occupied by a 30,000 square foot, three 
story, commercial office building. The Site abuts the Needham Line of the MBTA Commuter Rail 
System to the north, Baker Street to the east and the 60 unit Residences Off Baker housing 
development to the south (under construction). The proposed redevelopment would include a five 
story, 62,140 sf apartment building with approximately 55 units and 55 surface parking spaces. The 
building will also have 55 resident bicycle spaces inside the building and visitor bicycle spaces in 
conformance with the City guidelines. A generous landscape courtyard is planned that will link to an 
open space provided on an adjacent Residences Off Baker apartment building. The proposed building’s 
massing is designed to relate to this adjacent residential development and the surrounding context 
including providing steps back at the fifth floor to reduce the perceived massing. 
The site is in a Community Commercial (CC) zoning subdistrict of the West Roxbury Neighborhood 
Zoning District and is subject to the BPDA’s Large Project review process under Article 80 of the Code. 
Anticipated zoning relief is limited to a height variance and Conditional Use Permit for the residential 
use. 
The Proponent has been engaged with BPDA staff for over a year and modified the program and site 
design to address the Agency’s major concerns including providing a pedestrian connection to Baker 
Street. A formal public review with the abutting neighborhood will be initiated upon submission on an 
Expanded Project Notification Form.

Dear Chief Shen: 
Our office represents Bahlmann Capital Group LLC (the “Proponent”), as land use counsel for 
its proposed development project at 120-134 Hampden Street in the Newmarket neighborhood of 
Roxbury consisting of four (4) parcels of land totaling approximately 29,603 square feet (the “Project 
Site”). The Proponent proposes an adaptive reuse of the existing Iron Mountain storage facility at the 
134 Hampden Street portion of the Project Site from Records Warehouse to Self-Storage Warehouse, 
and with the addition of a small, approximately 5,313 square foot office/retail building at the 120 
Hampden Street portion of the Project Site (the “Proposed Project”). The purpose of this letter is to 
notify the Boston Planning Department (the “Planning Department”) of the Proponent’s intent to file a 
Project Notification Form (the “PNF”), pursuant to Article 80B of the City of Boston Zoning Code (the 
"Zoning Code”) and the Executive Order Relative to the Provision of Mitigation by Development 
Projects in Boston, as amended. See attached Figure 1 – Project Locus. 
 
Specifically, as part of the Proposed Project, the Proponent proposes a change of use of 
approximately 66,993 square feet of Gross Floor Area (“GFA”) of the existing building at the 134 
Hampden Street portion of the Project Site from the existing Records Warehouse Use to a Self-Storage 
Use, along with accompanying changes of use to a wine storage use of approximately 434 square feet of 
GFA and to a business use of approximately 2,544 square feet of GFA, as well as a new canopy for 
loading/unloading and a small new 600 square foot GFA management office for the Self-Storage Use, 
all on the 134 Hampden Street portion of the Project Site. Additionally, the Proposed Project further 
contemplates the new construction of an approximately 5,313 square foot GFA office/retail building at 
the 120 Hampden Street portion of the Project Site in order to better activate the street corner, including 
approximately 2,530 square feet of retail space on the first level and approximately 2,783 square feet of 
office space on the second level. 
The Proposed Project includes a technical change of use from Warehousing to Self-Storage (as a 
distinct type of Warehousing) under the newly enacted Newmarket 21st Century Industrial Zoning 
District and the Newmarket Creative Industrial Zoning Subdistrict of the Zoning Code. In this regard, 
although Warehousing (Indoor) is categorized as an Allowed Use, Self-Storage is categorized more 
specifically under the Warehousing (Indoor) category and is itemized as a Conditional Use pursuant to

the new Article 90 of the Zoning Code. Thus, pursuant to Article 80B-2.3(c), as the Proposed Project 
seeks to change the uses of a gross floor area of fifty thousand (50,000) or more square feet in the 
existing building at the Project Site, it is subject to the Planning Department’s Large Project Review 
requirements. 
 
Prior to submitting this Letter of Intent, and as part of its advisory review process with the 
Planning Department, the Proponent and its development team conducted preliminary outreach with 
nearby residents, community leadership and local elected officials, to introduce itself and the potential 
merits of the Proposed Project. We greatly appreciate their willingness to engage and collaborate in 
discussions together and look forward to continuing to work with these important constituencies, the 
Planning Department and prospective members of its Impact Advisory Group in the regulatory process 
to follow. 
 
Thank you, as always, for your time and consideration. Please do not hesitate to contact me 
should you have any questions or for more information. 
 
Very truly yours, 
 
 
 
Nicholas J. Zozula, Esq.

Dear Director Jemison: 
 
On behalf of KS Partners, and in accordance with the Mayor’s 
Executive Order Relative to the Provision of Mitigation by Development 
Projects in Boston, dated October 10, 2000, as amended, we are pleased to 
submit this Letter of Intent for a proposed project on an approximately 16,399 
square foot parcel located at 141 Portland Street and 222 Friend Street in the 
Bulfinch Triangle Neighborhood (the “Project Site”). 
 
The Project Site is currently developed with a three-story commercial 
building and approximately 32-space surface parking lot. KS Partners 
proposes to replace the existing structure and paved parking area with an 
eleven-story life science building. The proposed building will be 
approximately 160,195 sf (gross floor area) and will measure approximately 
170 feet to the top of its highest occupied floor, with a mechanical penthouse 
occupying less than 30% of the roof area (the “Project”). Because the Project 
Site has exceptional access to transit, no parking spaces will be provided 
within the Project; a fully enclosed loading area will be provided on the 
ground level of the Project. 
 
The Project incorporates numerous public realm enhancements, 
including elimination of approximately 109 feet of curb cuts on Portland and 
Friend Streets, a reduction in paved area, widening of adjacent sidewalks, 
addition of urban landscape elements, and the creation of new ground floor

retail spaces on Portland Street and at the corner of Friend Street and Valenti 
Way. In addition, the Project has been designed to reflect the BPDA’s draft 
Life Science Building Design Guidelines, including by prioritizing small floor 
plates, integrating mechanicals into the overall building design, and activating 
the street and public realm. 
 
The Project Site is located within the General Area of the Bulfinch 
Triangle Neighborhood District. We anticipate that the Project will require 
zoning relief for height and FAR, as well as approval pursuant to Article 32 
(Groundwater Conservation Overlay District). The Project has been designed 
to comply with the requirements of Article 25 (Coastal Flood Resilience 
Overlay District). 
 
During this post-pandemic time when many downtown employees are 
still working remotely, the Project’s proposed development of a new life 
sciences building with numerous onsite jobs will help renew the vibrancy of 
the Downtown North area. We look forward to working with you and your 
staff at the BPDA, the City of Boston, elected officials and the community on 
this exciting infill opportunity. Please do not hesitate to contact me with any 
questions or for more information.

Dear Director Jemison: 
Our office represents 100 Monmouth Street LLC (the “Proponent”), as land use counsel 
for its proposed multi-family residential redevelopment at the above referenced property site (the 
Site”). The purpose of this letter is to notify the Boston Planning and Development Agency (the 
“BPDA”) of the Proponent’s intent to file a Project Notification Form (the “PNF”), pursuant to 
Article 80-B of the City of Boston Zoning Code (the "Zoning Code”) and the Executive Order 
Relative to the Provision of Mitigation by Development Projects in Boston, as amended. 
The Proponent seeks to revitalize the non-conforming property site at the edge of Boston’s 
Audubon Circle neighborhood and adjacent to the Town of Brookline, with a new multi-family 
development that better conforms to its residential character, at a transit-oriented location along 
the MBTA’s Green Line and its nearby subway stations. The proposed project would raze and 
replace an outdated commercial parking garage with a new six (6) story residential building of 
approximately 91,000 gross square feet, including 90 units of market-rate and income-restricted 
housing, new and expanded sidewalks, improved pedestrian and vehicular access, and on-site 
garaged and surface parking to serve both the project’s new residents and the Proponent’s off-
street parking obligations for its long-existing abutting apartment building at 101 Monmouth 
Street, with the Town of Brookline (the “Project”). As part of the Article 80 Large Project Review 
process, the Proponent will also work with the BPDA and the MBTA on potential opportunities 
for a future pedestrian connection to the MBTA’s Green Line Fenway Station (“Fenway Station”). 
The Site consists of approximately 29,634 square feet land, which abuts the MBTA’s 
Fenway Station on its D branch, and within a block from its St. Mary’s St Station on the C branch. 
Its existing commercial parking garage is a non-descript structure, which occupies most of the 
Site’s asymmetrical shaped lot. See attached Figure 1 – Project Locus – Existing Conditions.

With over 50,000 square-feet of new construction in the Audubon Circle neighborhood, 
the Project requires the BPDA’s Large Project Review under Article 80B of the Zoning Code. The 
Proponent’s PNF will study its potential impacts on the surrounding community, including 
transportation analysis, assessments of air, noise and shadows; environmental, sustainability, 
infrastructure and historic resources. The Project is also governed by Article 61 and other sections 
of the Zoning Code at its location in the Multi-Family Residential (MFR) Zoning Subdistrict of 
the Audubon Circle Neighborhood District. To address its Use and Dimensional deviations with 
the Zoning Code, the Proponent intends to seek relief and approvals by the City’s Board of Appeal, 
as required for the Project. 
Prior to filing this LOI, the Proponent and its development team conducted preliminary 
outreach with the Audubon Circle Neighborhood Association and its neighboring property owners 
and local residents in the area, to seek their early input and feedback on the Project. This initial 
engagement process has helped to shape the values of the Project, and these important 
constituencies will continue to guide its resulting development program through the Article 80 
process with the BPDA. 
Thank you for your time and consideration, and we look forward to working with you and 
your staff, members of the to-be-formed Impact Advisory Group, local officials, abutting and 
nearby property owners, local residents and community at large on this exciting project. Please 
do not hesitate to contact me with any questions, or for more information. 
Very truly yours, 
Joseph P. Hanley, Esq.

Dear Director Jemison: 
 
On behalf of Mass Bay Credit Union (“MBCU”) and 29 A Street Realty Trust, our client 
Lincoln Property Company (the “Proponent” or “Lincoln”) is pleased to submit this Letter of Intent 
pursuant to the Mayor’s Executive Order of October 20, 2000, as amended, regarding a 
development proposal (the “Project”) at 139-147 West Fourth Street, 29 A Street, 259 Gold Street, 
and 10 West Fifth Street (the “Site” or “147 West Fourth Street”) in South Boston, within the area 
studied by the Boston Planning and Development Agency (the “BPDA”) in PLAN: South Boston 
Dorchester Avenue, published in December 2016 (the “Dorchester Avenue Plan”). 
As the current owners of the approximately 1.2-acre Site, MBCU and 29 A Street Realty 
Trust have partnered with Lincoln to purchase and redevelop the Site with a new headquarters 
bank facility for use by MBCU (the “MBCU Headquarters”), and so allow MBCU to remain 
anchored in the South Boston community, long into the future. 
In addition to a new, two-story, approximately 15,000 square-foot (“sf”) MBCU 
Headquarters, the Project would include a new, eight-story, approximately 113,000-sf office / 
laboratory building (the “Office / Lab Building”), and a new, 13-story, approximately 111,000-sf 
residential building (the “Residential Building”). Onsite parking for approximately 112 vehicles 
would be shared by all uses at the Site. 
The Project is subject to Large Project Review under Section 80B of the Boston Zoning 
Code, and the Proponent intends to file a Project Notification Form (“PNF”) within 90 days of this 
Letter of Intent. The Project is of such size that the Boston Civic Design Commission (“BCDC”) 
would normally review the architectural design.

Location 
The Site comprises five (5) parcels of land at the northeasterly corner of the intersection of 
A Street and Dorchester Avenue, in an historically industrial section of South Boston: 
• 139-147 West Fourth Street (Boston Assess. Dept. Parcel ID No. 0600164000); 
• A 925-sf portion of (non-highway) land currently owned by the Massachusetts 
Department of Transportation (Boston Assess. Dept. Parcel ID No. 0602769010); 
• 29 A Street (Boston Assess. Dept. Parcel ID No. 0600158000); 
• 259 Gold Street (Boston Assess. Dept. Parcel ID No. 0600189010); and 
• 10 West Fifth Street (Boston Assess. Dept. Parcel ID No. 0600189000). 
The Site has a combined lot area of approximately 53,459 square feet (1.2 acres). 
At present, the northeasterly corner of the Site is improved with a two-story bank and office 
building with a gross floor area (“GFA”) of approximately 13,000 sf that serves as the headquarters 
for the Mass Bay Credit Union. At the northwesterly end of the Site, the parcel at 19 A Street is 
improved with a one-to-two-story masonry building occupied by A Street Scrap Metals 
Corporation. The parcel known as 259 Gold Street is a private way, not open to public travel, and 
whose use is shared with the multifamily residential building at 20 West Fifth Street. The rest of 
the Site is paved parking, serving the current MBCU headquarters. 
Planning and Zoning 
As noted above, the Site is located within the area studied by the BPDA in the Dorchester 
Avenue Plan, published in December 2016. Also, the Site is located within the underlaying M-1 
(Restricted Manufacturing) zoning district, as well as the Restricted Parking Overlay District. 
(Boston Zoning Map 4 [South Boston].) The Site is eligible to be established as a PDA because it 
contains not less than one acre. 
Use, Size, and General Description 
Through the Project, Lincoln would merge the five parcels comprising the Site into a single 
lot of approximately 53,459 sf, raze all existing improvements, and construct in their place three 
buildings with a combined GFA of approximately 239,000 sf, and so an overall floor area ratio 
(“FAR”) of approximately 4.5. 
Similar to MBCU’s existing headquarters building, but relocated to the corner of A Street 
and West Fifth Street, with its westerly façade toward Dorchester Avenue, the proposed MBCU 
Headquarters would be two-stories high, with a building height of approximately 30 feet, and a 
GFA of approximately 15,000 sf.

The proposed Office / Lab Building would be built in place of today’s MBCU headquarters, 
facing West Fourth Street, and Lincoln would own and manage it. It would have eight stories, 
rising approximately 125 feet above grade, with its fifth through eighth stories set back from West 
Fourth Street, and a mechanical penthouse, set back still farther, that meets the BPDA’s pending 
design standards for life sciences projects. Total GFA would be approximately 113,000 sf. 
The proposed Residential Building would rise at the corner of West Fourth Street and A 
Street, and would also be owned and managed by Lincoln. It would have a building height of 
approximately 147 feet, with shorter floor-to-ceiling heights than the proposed Office / Lab 
Building, for a total of 13 stories. Its seventh through 13th stories would be set back from both 
West Fourth Street and A Street, matching the upper-story setbacks of the Office / Lab building. 
The Residential Building would have a GFA of approximately 111,000 sf, including 
approximately 2,500 sf of ground-level retail / services / restaurant space. Twenty percent (20%) 
of residential square footage would be set aside as affordable housing, per the Mayor’s proposed 
revision to Boston’s Inclusionary Development Policy (“IDP”). 
Large Project Review 
Because it would involve new construction with a gross floor area of at least 50,000 square 
feet within a neighborhood zoning district, the Project is subject to the Boston Zoning Code’s 
Large Project Review process, administered by the BPDA. As noted above, the Proponent intends 
to file a Project Notification Form within the next 90 days. 
Zoning Relief 
Office buildings and banks [Use No. 41], research laboratories [Use No. 48], local retail 
[Use No. 34], general retail at the small size proposed [Use No. 35], and eating and drinking 
establishments [Use No. 37] are all permitted by right in the M-1 zoning district. (Boston Zoning 
Code § 8-7, Table A.) Multi-family dwellings, however, normally require a conditional use permit 
in the M-1 zoning district, from the Boston Board of Appeal. Although the proposed building 
heights and FAR are consistent with the Dorchester Avenue Plan, they also require zoning relief. 
Conclusion 
MBCU and 29 A Street Realty Trust have partnered with Lincoln Property Company to 
purchase and redevelop the Site with a new headquarters bank facility for use by MBCU. 
Accompanied by new office / lab and multifamily residential buildings, this will allow MBCU to 
remain anchored in the South Boston community, long into the future.

Dear Chief Jemison: 
TC Boston Development Inc, a subsidiary of the Trammel Crow Company, in partnership with 
The Community Builders, is excited to file this Letter of Intent for the redevelopment of a 
collective 7 acres of land on a stretch of Soldiers Field Road in Brighton that today remains a 
vestige of the past. The proposed redevelopment is anticipated to take place in two phases, with 
adjacent parcels: the first phase consists of 1600 Soldiers Field Road and 15 Soldiers Field Place, 
and the second phase would include 1800 & 1850 Soldiers Field Road. Collectively, the 
development project will deliver to the community two residential buildings that will be 100% 
affordable at an average cost of 60% AMI, supported by three commercial buildings including 
lab, office, and retail. In coordination with DCR, the project will also include significant 
improvements to the Leo M. Birmingham Park and Parkway to which the project site is 
immediately adjacent, as well as improvements to the I-90 underpasses that, today, fail to provide 
a safe or aesthetically pleasing connection between the neighborhoods and the Charles River, that 
have been separated by the Massachusetts Turnpike for decades. 
The affordable housing buildings in the project will contain 65% two and three-bedroom units 
aimed at providing affordable living spaces for Boston’s families and will average 60% AMI – 
true affordability. The 200 affordable units in this one redevelopment project would 
approximately double the number of “IDP” units provided by a dozen other projects, collectively, 
in the immediate Allston-Brighton neighborhood over the last several years, and will be provided 
at deeper levels of affordability than the majority of those other units. 
The commercial piece of the development will support the affordable housing components. After 
completing the infrastructure required to support the residential structures, The Trammell Crow 
Company will donate the land upon which The Community Builders will build the affordable 
housing. The development team will also be requesting the City of Boston to direct the affordable 
housing linkage payments due from the commercial development to The Community Builders to 
help fund the deeply affordable housing units. 

The area of the proposed redevelopment is blighted and decadent, lacking sponsorship, financial 
investment or improvement, any community activation, and has increasingly become a beacon for 
unwanted and illegal activities. The redevelopment sites include a car dealership and associated 
surface parking lot, an HVAC contractor’s facility, the International House of Pancakes, 
originally built in 1960, and the former Charles River Inn motel property built in 1955. These 
properties have remained effectively untouched and unimproved since the 1950’s and 1960’s, 
despite their gateway location at the origin of Soldiers Field Road and running alongside the 
Charles River. 
The Project, which will be approximately 1 million square feet, will be proposed as an M.G.L. c. 
121A project and an Article 80C Master Plan Development Area in order to reset the zoning on 
this single block stretch of Soldiers Field Road that was left out of the Western Avenue planning 
efforts that, as recently adopted, up-zoned the remainder of Soldiers Field Road/Western Avenue 
corridor to a 4.25 FAR and 185 feet in height, with incentives. This proposal will be consistent 
with the recently adopted Western Avenue corridor to which it is immediately adjacent. 
Trammel Crow and The Community Builders look forward to working closely with the Boston 
Planning and Development Agency and the City of Boston to advance this vision and bring 
significant and important affordable housing and other public space benefits to the 
Allston/Brighton neighborhoods.

The Project Site is located entirely within Planned Development Area No. 69, South Boston/The 
100 Acres that was approved as a Master Plan PDA on January 10, 2007(as the same has been 
amended, the “Master Plan”). The Project Site includes historic tidelands that are subject to Chapter 91 
licensing and use requirements under M.G.L. c. 91 and its implementing regulations and the South 
Boston Municipal Harbor Plan. 
 
The Proponent intends to develop a portion of the Project Site into a single-building mixed-use 
development of approximately 455,000 square feet of gross floor area, including laboratory/R&D, office,

improvements along the Fort Point Channel (the “Project”). The parking needs of the Project are expected 
to be served primarily by a below-grade garage beneath the proposed building, which will replace the 125 
surface parking spaces presently existing at the Project Site. The Project is proposed to be constructed in 
accordance with the use requirements and is proposed to exceed the minimum open space requirements, 
set forth in the Master Plan. The remaining redevelopment potential of the Project Site under the Master 
Plan is 485,608 square feet of new gross floor area, as stated in the Sixth Amendment to the Master Plan 
dated October 13, 2022; the Proponent will seek approximately 455,000 square feet of gross floor area 
within the Project.

parking and staging area for delivery and operations of the abutting Gillette Company manufacturing 
facility. The Proponent, working with local architectural team at Payette, intends to transform the 
underutilized Project Site into a vibrant, inclusive mixed-use project that integrates into and complements

On behalf of Tishman Speyer ERC Developer, L.L.C. (the “Proponent”), we are pleased to submit this Letter of Intent 
("LOI") to file a Project Notification Form (“PNF”) for Phase B of the Enterprise Research Campus (ERC) Project (“Phase B”, 
the “Phase B Project”) located on an approximately 4.8-acre parcel at 100 Western Avenue in the Allston neighborhood 
(the “Project Site”). This Letter of Intent is being submitted in accordance with the Mayor’s Executive Order dated 
October 10, 2000, as amended on April 3, 2001, and Article 80 of the City of Boston Zoning Code. 
 
The Project Site is located within Planned Development Area No. 115 that was approved as a Master Plan PDA by the 
Boston Zoning Commission ("BZC") on March 15, 2018 and is governed by the Amended and Restated Master Plan for 
Planned Development Area No. 115 adopted by BZC on August 10, 2022 (the “Amended and Restated Master Plan”). The 
Phase B Project represents the second phase of the larger ERC located in the Allston Landing North Economic 
Development Area. Previously, the Proponent sought approval for the initial phase of the Enterprise Research Campus 
(the "Phase A Project") and, following an extensive community engagement process, which included discussion and 
analysis of the Phase B Project, the Proponent received BPDA approval for the Phase A Project (the "Phase A Project 
Approvals"). While it will undergo a dedicated Article 80 process, the Phase B Project will build on many of the successful 
urban design, public realm and programming concepts established in the Phase A Project. 
 
The Project Site has historically contained industrial and transportation uses and will be utilized as a construction staging 
and logistics area for the Phase A Project until construction of the Phase B Project commences. Consistent with the Phase 
B Project described in the Phase A PNF, in the Phase A Draft Project Impact Report (“DPIR”), and in public meetings, the 
Proponent is proposing a Phase B Project consisting of approximately 720,000 sf of laboratory/R&D and office uses and 
approximately 320,000 sf of residential uses, with a mixture of ground floor retail and community uses. Additionally, 
Phase B is proposed to include above-grade and below-grade parking spaces to support the Phase B Project and parking 
spaces granted as part of the Phase A Project Approvals.

studied as part of the transportation impact study for the Phase A Project. Phase B is subject to full Article 80 review, and

Amended and Restated Master Plan and Article 80C of the Zoning Code.

including the Phase A Project’s commitments to sustainability and to Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (DEI). The Phase B

additional ground floor active uses, further establishing the ERC as a vibrant, mixed-use development that is inclusive and 
welcoming to all.

Oxford Properties Group and Pappas Enterprises, Inc. (collectively “OxP”) is pleased to 
submit this Letter of Intent to initiate the regulatory review process for a mixed-use development 
(the “Project”) on approximately 8 acres of land along West First and E Streets and along Pappas 
Way (the “Project Site”). The Project Site is part of the 42-acre business park, of which OxP is 
the owner-operator, located between Summer and West First Streets, and along E Street, Pappas 
Way and the Reserved Channel in South Boston (“OxP Property”). By way of background, Oxford 
Properties Group and Pappas Enterprises, Inc. partnered together to form a joint venture in 2019 
related to the OxP Property. OxP operates the Property under a long-term lease with the 
Massachusetts Port Authority (“Massport”) that Pappas Enterprises, Inc. has held through various 
affiliates since 1965, as well as by fee ownership of certain adjoining land areas. 
Beginning in 2019, OxP began to reach out to local residents and property owners, 
neighborhood leadership, and the South Boston community, for the purpose of introducing them 
to the new joint venture and seeking their early input and guidance on long-term visioning and 
potential future master planning of the Project Site and the OxP Property. To date, this preliminary 
engagement process has included over fifty (50) meetings in the community and five (5) 
community-centered charettes, which focused on public realm, resiliency and mobility, urban 
design, and how the community can connect to and benefit from simple interventions with open 
space and the potential transformation of this area. We deeply value the time and feedback, and 
our team looks forward to continuing to closely collaborate with the community. 
The OxP Property existing conditions include nine (9) industrial and commercial buildings, 
open-air surface parking lots, and a much-improved pedestrian route with historical signage and 
open green space along the waterfront of Reserved Channel. Of its total area of 42 acres, 
approximately 38.2 acres are ground leased from Massport, while the other 3.4 acres are fee-owned 
by OxP. There are existing leases on various buildings on the OxP Property, some of which do not 

 
expire for 15+ years. The Project Site includes approximately 6.2 acres ground leased from 
Massport and 1.7 acres fee owned by OxP, and existing lease agreements allow for redevelopment 
to move forward in the next few years. We propose to redevelop the Project with a shared 
community vision for creating an inclusive and vibrant development that connects to the 
neighborhood in thoughtful ways and invests in creating spaces where new and current neighbors 
and businesses can thrive together. 
Specifically, the Project envisions improved and expanded public sidewalks along its 
sections of First Street which borders the residential area, with thoughtfully designed open spaces, 
high quality landscaping, and new building heights and massing that respect and connect with the 
adjacent South Boston residential neighborhood. The Project is proposed to include approximately 
1.7 million square feet of development in 7 new buildings, of which approximately 1.1 million 
square feet is anticipated to be located on the approximately 6 acres of land along West First Street 
and approximately 600,000 square feet along Pappas Way. Proposed building uses would include 
a variety of commercial and employment-based opportunities, with a portion of residential housing 
that responds to the needs of the neighborhood. Visioning for ground floor uses could include a 
neighborhood grocery store, new fitness, and wellness options for the neighborhood and locally 
owned eateries, with a building massing and heights calibrated to respect the existing structures 
along First Street and the residential section of South Boston, and with increasing building heights 
moving north, away from West First Street. 
Understanding the importance of multi-modal connectivity, sustainability and resiliency, 
and community planning, OxP will provide a conceptual framework for transportation solutions, 
resilient infrastructure, public open space and other important elements that will be necessary to 
support the future build-out of the overall OxP Property; future proposed development of the OxP 
Property outside of the Project Site would be reviewed through future regulatory filings. The 
Project will fit into this planning framework that will accommodate a phased development and 
allow for proposals for the OxP Property to evolve over time in response to community interests 
and market conditions. 
OxP aims to create meaningful and positive improvements to the community, and this is 
embedded in the principles and goals of the Project. OxP will continue to make diversity, equity, 
and inclusion (“DE&I”) a pinnacle focus through the development of the Project and during all 
phases of the Project. 
As the Project Site includes a mix of both land ground leased from Massport and land 
owned in fee by OxP, a portion of the Project will require the City of Boston’s (“City”) adoption 
of a Planned Development Area (“PDA”) Development Plan, under Section 80C of the Zoning 
Code, along with the BPDA’s Large Project Review under Article 80B of the same. Although the 
land ground leased from Massport is not subject to the City’s regulatory review and approvals 
process, we intend to voluntarily undertake various components of Large Project Review for this 
portion of the Project Site as well, consistent with the regulatory approach taken by many other 
development projects on Massport land. Specifically, our plan is to file a Project Notification 
Form for the Project in the coming months, as necessary to commence the regulatory review 

process with the BPDA, and to begin to engage in the formal public review process with an Impact 
Advisory Group (“IAG”), area residents, and neighborhood leadership. 
Thank you for your time and consideration, and we look forward to working with 
Massport, the BPDA, and the South Boston community on the proposed Project. Please do not 
hesitate to contact us with any questions, or for any additional information.
